definition: A very large neural network, typically a Transformer, trained on massive text to predict and generate language.
details: LLMs learn statistical patterns of language and code from enormous corpora, and at scale display abilities such as instruction following, reasoning and tool use. A survey of the field maps their architecture, training, adaptation and evaluation, and describes the tuning, alignment and prompting techniques that turn a text predictor into an assistant.

explainer.lead: A large language model is a very large neural network, typically a Transformer, trained on massive text to predict and generate language. At scale these models show instruction following, reasoning and tool use, and tuning and alignment turn a text predictor into an assistant.

tiers.eli5: It's a giant pattern-finder that has read enormous amounts of text and learned to guess what comes next, well enough to hold a conversation.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply prompting, tuning and alignment techniques to adapt a base text predictor into a useful assistant. A pitfall is expecting those abilities for free: they emerge from scale and adaptation, and a survey of the field maps architecture, training, adaptation and evaluation to keep expectations grounded.
tiers.paperLevel: An LLM is a very large neural network, typically a Transformer, trained on massive corpora to predict and generate language by learning statistical patterns of language and code. Its abilities at scale are described empirically rather than guaranteed.

explainer.example: Given a user instruction, an LLM trained on massive text generates a step-by-step answer and can call an external tool when prompted to do so.

citation.title: A Survey of Large Language Models
